To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effective diameter as a fetch parameter is not appropriate to be used as a substitute for the physical fetch in emission models for wastewater treatment plants.
the effective diameter should not be used as the fetch parameter in models of odorous emissions from wastewater treatment plants, as the deviations introduced are potentially large.

The deviations in the calculation of mass transfer coefficients at passive liquid surfaces, due to the use of the conceptually inappropriate effective diameter as fetch in the calculation of K0, are significantly larger for the volatilisation of liquid phase dominated compounds than for gas phase dominated compounds, and the use of the physical fetch shall be recommended for the calculation of K 0 in emission models for wastewater treatment plants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the conceptually appropriate physical fetch as a parameter in the calculation the mass transfer coefficient for passive liquid surfaces at WWTPs.
a sensitivity analysis of the WATER9 model for the estimation of emissions of odorous pollutants from passive liquid surfaces at WWTPs.
the development of a new method to estimate the mass transfer coefficient for passive liquid surfaces at WWTPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effective diameter as a fetch parameter in the WATER9 model is not recommended for the calculation of mass transfer coefficients for passive liquid surfaces at WWTPs.

the use of an effective fetch parameter in emission models for passive liquid surfaces at WWTPs is not recommended, as this approach may lead to significant systematic deviations in the model predictions.

the use of effective diameter instead of fetch length in the calculation of mass transfer coefficients in emission models of passive liquid surfaces at WWTPs is not recommended for a varied range and configurations of wind speeds and WWTPs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of an effective diameter in the calculation of mass transfer coefficients at passive liquid surfaces in wastewater treatment plants is not recommended, as it can lead to significant errors in the estimation of the emissions.

the present study shows that the use of an appropriate fetch parameter for the calculation of mass transfer coefficients at passive liquid surfaces present at WWTPs is essential for the development of accurate and reliable models.

the use of a simplified approach to calculate the mass transfer coefficient at wastewater treatment plant passive liquid surfaces may introduce large systematic deviations in the predictions of odour emission models.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of an empirical model, such as the WATER9 model for estimating the emissions from wastewater treatment plants, requires a careful analysis of the model assumptions and limitations in order to avoid the introduction, by model calibration, of large systematic deviations.

the use of effective diameter as fetch length in the calculation of mass transfer coefficient in emission models for odorous compounds from WWTPs can lead to significant deviations in model predictions.
, in general, the effective diameter should not be used as fetch parameter in models for the calculation of mass transfer coefficients for odorous compounds at wastewater treatment plants.
